NUMBER 14. YEAR 2008
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
1. GENERAL ELUCIDATION
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and the homeland of Indonesia.
Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.
Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.
Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-esteem must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.
. From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 5
Every victim has the right to report and receive assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

Article 4
Article 5
Article 6
What is meant by obtaining protection is obtaining protection from family, the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the Court, Advocates, Social Institutions or other parties either temporarily or based on the determination of a protection order from the court, husband, wife and children.
What is meant by obtaining information is knowing about the existence of complaint centers, P2T-P2A and or other competent supporting institutions regarding matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and the development of case handling.
What is meant by integrated services are services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial, legal and socio-political. What is meant by continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of good name and the victim has the right to obtain socio-economic empowerment.
What is meant by the victim having the right to report is that the victim can report acts of violence to the Secretariat of P2T-P2A Jombang Regency or Jombang Police Resort (UPPA), or Women's Crisis Center (WCC) Jombang, What is meant by obtaining psychological and legal assistance is obtaining psychological and legal assistance at every level of examination and throughout the judicial process.
Sufficiently clear

Article 3
The best interests of the victim are all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.
What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men and all actions that deprive children of their rights and freedoms.

Article 3
The purpose of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence that is based on gender and the best interests of women and children.

Article 2
Number 1 Respect for the rights of victims is intended for the fulfillment of the rights of victims.
Number 2 } Gender justice is a process to become fair toward men and women;
# Number 3 Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, national defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of such development.
Number 4 Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

1.5.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation defines violence only generally (Pasal 1 angka 8) and then specifies physical (angka 9), psychological (angka 10), and sexual violence (angka 11). There is no explicit category of “kekerasan ekonomi” / economic violence, economic exploitation, deprivation/neglect of economic resources, etc. The General Elucidation mentions “keamanan ... ekonomi” (economic security) as something the state should protect, and the Elucidation of Pasal 4 mentions “pemberdayaan sosial ekonomi” as part of rehabilitation/empowerment, but neither constitutes defining or addressing economic violence as a form of violence. Therefore the judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the Indonesian text; the golden ‘Yes’ appears incorrect.

1.9.evaluator_rationale: Although sexual violence is defined, the candidate sentences do not explicitly include sexual exploitation or sexual slavery as specific forms addressed by the policy.

1.9.rationale: The Indonesian text defines “kekerasan seksual” in Pasal 1 angka 11 as sexual harassment and coercion of sexual relations, including “baik untuk tujuan komersial dan/atau tujuan tertentu.” This covers coercion/harassment and possibly commercial sexual acts, but the regulation does not explicitly mention trafficking, sexual exploitation as a distinct form, or sexual slavery (perbudakan seksual).
